title: Tottenham ends 8½-year Stamford Bridge drought with 2-0 win - CHOSUNBIZ
text:
Tottenham ends 8½-year Stamford Bridge drought with 2-0 win - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 10월 26일(월) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports Tottenham ends 8½-year Stamford Bridge drought with 2-0 win 
 입력 2026.10.25. 07:00 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Tottenham Hotspur finally broke their jinx at Chelsea's ground. Taking advantage of a costly mistake by the opposing goalkeeper and a clinching goal from Matisse Thiel, they secured a victory at Stamford Bridge for the first time in 8 years and 6 months.
 Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham defeated Chelsea 2-0 in an away match in the eighth round of the 2026-2027 English Premier League at Stamford Bridge in London, England, on the 25th (Korea time).
 With this, Tottenham registered their second straight win of the season following a 3-1 victory over Coventry City in the previous match. They moved up to 12th in the league with nine points (2 wins, 3 draws, 3 losses).
 Above all, the victory is significant because it came away at Chelsea. Tottenham had not won at Stamford Bridge since April 2018, about 8 years and 6 months ago. It was the first time since then, when Christian Eriksen's equalizer and Dele Alli's multi-goal performance produced a 3-1 comeback win.
 Tottenham lined up in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Omar Marmoushi occupied the front line, with Matisse Thiel, James Maddison and Mohammed Kudus positioned on the second line. Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes formed the midfield, and Andy Robertson, Micky van der Ven, Jan Paul van Hecker and Archie Gray composed the back line. The goal was guarded by Antonin Kinský.
 Chelsea responded with a 3-4-2-1 formation. Morgan Rogers led the front, supported in attack by Cole Palmer and Giovani Kenda. Jorell Hato, Jordan Henderson, Moisés Caicedo and Pedro Neto occupied the midfield. Levi Colwill, Maxence Lacroix and Josh Acheampong formed the defense, and Mike Penders wore the goalkeeper's gloves.
 Early in the match Chelsea created the first chance. In the 15th minute of the first half, Palmer attempted a left-footed curling shot inside the penalty area, but Kinský's save stopped it.
 Tottenham responded. In the 29th minute of the first half, Marmoushi, who received Robertson's cutback, struck a right-footed shot in the box, but Penders saved it.
 In the 35th minute of the first half, Chelsea capitalized on a passing error by Kinský to create a chance. Henderson attempted a shot from outside the penalty area, but Kinský threw himself to make the save and redeemed his mistake.
 The first half ended 0-0.
 Tottenham suffered a setback early in the second half. In the 6th minute of the second half, Maddison went down complaining of pain and was replaced by Conor Gallagher.
 Both teams used substitutions to make changes. In the 20th minute of the second half, Tottenham withdrew Robertson and Marmoushi and brought on Pedro Porro and Dominic Solanke.
 The tense balance was broken in the 32nd minute of the second half. From a corner delivered by Fernandes, Chelsea goalkeeper Penders attempted to punch the ball clear. However, the ball struck his hand incorrectly and went into the net. It was an own goal by Penders. Tottenham went ahead 1-0.
 Chelsea suffered a bigger blow. In the 35th minute of the second half, Palmer received a second booking for a foul stepping on Gallagher's ankle. Having been booked earlier, Palmer was eventually sent off for accumulation of bookings.
 Having secured a numerical advantage, Tottenham put the result beyond doubt.
 In the 42nd minute of the second half, Thiel collected the ball on the left flank and drove centrally. After beating a defender, he unleashed a powerful right-footed shot from outside the penalty area, and the ball was sucked into the lower left corner of the net.
 The score was 2-0. It was a decisive goal that broke Chelsea's will to chase.
 Tottenham held the two-goal lead until seven minutes into stoppage time in the second half to confirm the victory. Tottenham also led in the statistics. They recorded an expected goals (xG) of 0.74, outpacing Chelsea (0.43).
 This victory means more than just three points. Tottenham, which had struggled early in the season, found a springboard for recovery with two consecutive wins. Above all, breaking the jinx at Chelsea, where they had not won for a long time, gave them confidence.
 By contrast, Chelsea collapsed at home amid the own goal by the goalkeeper and Palmer's dismissal. They suffered their first home defeat under manager Xabi Alonso, halting their upward momentum.
